basil.note: Frost-tender annual picked through the warm months; tropical gardens grow it all year, desert growers avoid midsummer heat and winter, boreal ones grow it under glass.

celery_leaves.note: Leafy celery tops follow the celery crop: a cool-season harvest in warm climates, summer into autumn where winters are cold.

chervil.note: Delicate cool-season annual that bolts in heat: picked in spring and autumn in temperate gardens and through the mild winter further south.

chives.note: Hardy perennial onion that resprouts in early spring and is cut until autumn frosts; hot summers slow it down in warmer zones.

coriander_leaf.note: Fast annual that bolts in heat: a winter crop from India and China to the Mediterranean and the US South, a summer one in cool northern gardens.

curry_leaf.note: Evergreen tropical tree picked all year in South India and South-East Asia; in cooler frost-free places it sheds or stalls over winter.

dill.note: A summer herb in Northern and Eastern Europe; in the Mediterranean, Middle East and South Asia it is sown in autumn and cut through winter and spring.

epazote.note: Pungent Mexican herb that grows almost like a weed all year in warm Mexico and Central America; at the subtropical edge it is a summer annual.

fenugreek_leaf.note: Methi leaves are a winter crop in India and Pakistan, cut young a few weeks after sowing; cooler countries grow them in summer.

lavender.note: Flower spikes are cut in early to midsummer when the first buds open, from Provence and Bulgaria to English and Hokkaido lavender fields.

lemon_balm.note: Hardy perennial in the mint family, cut from spring until autumn; young leaves before flowering have the cleanest lemon scent.

lemon_verbena.note: Deciduous South American shrub that leafs out in late spring and is picked until autumn; it is tender in hard frost.

lemongrass.note: Tropical perennial grass cut all year in South-East Asia; in warm temperate places stalks are harvested from summer until the first cold.

lovage.note: Tall hardy perennial whose young leaves and stalks are best in spring and early summer, before it flowers; a cool-climate herb.

marjoram.note: Tender perennial cut several times from spring to autumn in Egypt and the Mediterranean; northern growers treat it as a summer annual.

mint.note: Spreading perennial cut from spring to late autumn; it dies back in cold winters but grows all year in the tropics and in irrigated desert fields.

oregano.note: Hardy perennial whose leaves are best from late spring until just after it flowers in early summer; desert gardens get spring and autumn flushes.

parsley.note: Frost-tolerant biennial: picked all year in mild Mediterranean fields, in the cool season where summers are hot, and from late spring to autumn up north.

rosemary.note: Evergreen shrub picked all year where winters are mild; it rarely survives continental winters outdoors, so there it is a summer crop.

sage.note: Evergreen subshrub with soft new leaves from spring to autumn; growth stalls in winter, and in hot deserts it is a cool-season herb.

sorrel.note: Hardy perennial whose sharp young leaves come in spring, with a second flush in autumn where summers are not too harsh.

summer_savory.note: Warm-season annual sown after frost and cut through summer, best just as it starts to flower; a classic bean herb in Central Europe and the Balkans.

tarragon.note: French tarragon is a perennial that sprouts in spring and dies back in autumn; it dislikes hot, humid summers.

thai_basil.note: Heat-loving basil grown all year in tropical South-East Asia; elsewhere it is a frost-tender summer crop.

thyme.note: Evergreen subshrub cut from spring, around its flowering, into autumn; winter cold and desert summer heat halt its growth.
